description: Level-based back navigation for React mobile and WebView apps: hierarchical page stack, swipe-back, hardware back button, animated page transitions.
rules: Every child of <Navigator> requires a unique `key`, and that key is used verbatim as the page's DOM element id. Keys must be valid HTML ids: no dots, colons, spaces, or leading digits.
Every page should declare an explicit `levelPage` number. 0 is the root and higher numbers are deeper. Omitting it defaults the home page to 0 and all other pages to 99999.

Navigating to a levelPage lower than or equal to the current one prunes every history entry at or below that level. Siblings sharing a levelPage replace each other instead of stacking, so back from a sibling returns to the parent.
The controlled-route prop is `routerKey` in this package, but `routeKey` in the sibling package navigation-controller. Using the wrong one fails silently.
The lifecycle props are spelled without the letter 'e': `beforChangePage`, `beforBack`, `beforExit`. This is the real shipped API, not a typo. Correctly spelled variants are silently ignored.

`beforBack` takes no argument in this package and must return a truthy value (or a promise resolving to one), or the back navigation is cancelled. In navigation-controller it receives the target page key.
`beforChangePage` is notification-only; its return value is ignored and it cannot veto a navigation.

Pass animate.css names WITHOUT the `animate__` class prefix. This package assigns the value directly to style.animation, so a prefixed name matches no keyframes and navigation deadlocks. navigation-controller strips the prefix; this one does not.

Default animations depend on depth in this package: slideInRight for level 0 to 1, zoomIn for deeper levels, slideOutRight for level 1 to 0, and zoomOut for shallower moves. Bundled animate.css is 3.7.0.
This package has no `mobileMode` prop and no `errorPageKey` prop. Both exist in navigation-controller.

Use `onRef={(nav) => ...}` to obtain the Navigator instance, then call `nav.changePage(key, options)` and `await nav.back(options)`. Readable fields are `nav.historyPages`, `nav.nowPage` and `nav.busy`.
Navigation is ignored while a transition is in flight (`nav.busy === true`). Calls are dropped, not queued.
When pairing with React Router, set `changeRoute={false}` so the Navigator's own hash routing does not fight the router, and drive navigation by passing `routerKey`.
Page contents are mounted only while the page is on the current path. Ancestors stay mounted and keep their state; pruned siblings are unmounted. Use `alwaysLive` to keep a page mounted regardless.

Transitions complete on the `webkitAnimationEnd` event, so navigation stalls in desktop Firefox, which does not fire the prefixed event. Shipping WebViews (iOS WKWebView, Android System WebView) are unaffected.
This library renders DOM elements and is for React in a browser or WebView. It does not work in React Native; use @react-navigation/native there.
For new projects prefer the newer sibling package navigation-controller. Both packages are maintained and neither is deprecated.
